jobs.title: Chief Strategy Officer - Part-time
jobs.description:
**About Birch Housing**

Join a team of dedicated people committed to fostering social equity by providing affordable housing to those who need it and providing opportunity for all through housing because everyone deserves a safe and quality place to call home.

Birch Housing is one of the largest private non\-profit community housing providers in Ontario. Formerly the Inter Faith Homes Group, we have a 45\-year history of helping our tenants reach their full potential through housing.

We own and manage 512 units in townhouses and apartment buildings in four cities in Greater Toronto. Approximately 50% of our rental units are for people who qualify for a rent\- geared\-to\-income subsidy. The other 50% are available for rent at the market rate. We are committed to creating great experiences for our tenants and making sure we meet their needs every day. We listen to them and work with our partners to create supportive communities for all who call Birch Housing their home.

For more information, visit: birchhousing.ca

**About this Amazing Opportunity**

This position is pivotal providing strategic advice to the Board and the Committees of the Board by supporting Birch Housing’s high\-priority initiatives including Board governance, compliance, and building relationships with Service Managers. They also play a critical role in assisting in the development of the strategic plan, identifying strategic partnerships and opportunities and implementation of the strategic plan.

**Your Responsibilities**

* Act as a professional advisor to the Board and Committees and prepare and review reports to ensure all corporate and legal requirements are met.
* Aid in the development of the strategic plan and its implementation.
* Lead and build strategic relationships with Service Managers across all areas, sharing key information about Birch Housing’s strategic plan, needs and opportunities and defining opportunities to align our goals with funding partners.
* Ensure Board and Committee records, by\-laws, operational and Board policies, insurance policies, essential contracts, Service Manager directions, etc. are available and up to date.
* Ensure the Corporation is meeting all legal and mandated requirements, including those that are the responsibility of the Property Manager.
* Monitor emerging legislative, regulatory, funding and sector developments and advise the Board of their potential implications for Birch Housing.
* Identify, evaluate and implement measures to control the organizational risk to include human capital (Board Members, tenants, employees), property, finances, goodwill, and reputation.
* Ensure that standard business processes and procedures are in place and followed.
* Lead in collaboration with the Controller the long\-term financial strategy to support projects as they move out of current funding agreements, including negotiations with Service Managers and other funders.
* Identify and leverage potential partnerships with private, not\-for\-profit or public sector that align with Birch Housing’s vision and negotiate those partnerships that have potential for mutual benefit.
* Research, identify, leverage and prepare funding and lending applications in collaboration with the Property Management Company.
* Participate in occasional engagement with tenants pertaining to critical issues.
* Ensure that Birch Housing operates with legality and conformity to established regulations.
* Other duties as assigned.

**What you Bring to the Role**

* Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy or related field.
* Chartered Member of the Chartered Institute of Housing (or similar). Asset Management, Business Strategy, Property Management, and Human Resources training are assets.
* Minimum eight (8\) years of previous experience in a leadership role and equivalent experience in the public sector, specifically in housing.
* Exceptional communications and relationship\-building skills, with both internal and external partners.
* Ability to influence effectively.
* Strong partnership and collaboration skills.
* Strong financial acumen and strong compliance and regulatory knowledge is an asset.
* Extensive experience developing strategy, plans, and enhancing processes.
* Knowledge of Residential Tenancies Act, Landlord and Tenant Board, Human Rights legislation, and Housing Services Act.
* Extensive experience developing strategy, plans, and enhancing processes.
* Superior organizational skills with outstanding ability to attend to details and meet tight deadlines.
* Advanced MS Office Suite and knowledge of NewViews.
* Ability to travel within the GTA.

**Applying to the Role**

In order to be considered, please email your resume and cover letter to birchhousing@enlivenhr.ca

All applications must include the following information in the subject line:

**Application Deadline is Wednesday, November 18, 2026\.**

We thank all applicants for their interest in the role, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. If contacted for an interview, please inform us if you require accommodation.

In the spirit of the Human Rights Code, we ask that resumes do not include personal data including, but not limited to age, health, marital and family status.

As an employer committed to the principles of employment equity, we encourage applications from all persons including Black, Indigenous and people of colour, persons with disabilities, and persons of all sexual orientations and gender identities. We are committed to providing an inclusive and barrier free experience to applicants with accessibility needs in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code (2015\) and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA).

For candidates with disabilities requiring an accommodation, you may contact birchhousing@enlivenhr.ca

Pay: From $101,300\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* On\-site parking
* Work from home

Application question(s):

* Please detail your experience collaboratin

jobs.title: Director, Payments & Financial Services
jobs.description:
**About FreshBooks**


You've probably learned a bit about FreshBooks before making it to this point, but let us take a moment to introduce ourselves: At FreshBooks, we believe that small business owners are the backbone of the economy, yet they are often the most underserved when it comes to technology. For over 20 years, we’ve been on a mission to support owners, from the scrappy solopreneur with a big dream to the growing business with employees to manage.

  

Our leading platform is more than just business software; it’s an all\-in\-one financial toolkit that automates invoicing, expenses, payments and payroll, allowing our customers to spend less time on paperwork and more time doing the work they love.

  

We believe in human\-centric connections that empower teams to do their best work. Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, our team operates in clusters across North America and Europe using a variety of working environments \- remote, hybrid, and in\-office \- all based on what’s best for the team, collaboration, and mental well\-being. We are committed to creating a supportive and flexible workplace where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact on the lives of small business owners worldwide.

 **About the role**


The Director, Payments \& Financial Services is a senior leadership role within the Payments and Financial Services Line of Business, reporting directly to the General Manager, Financial Services and Payments. With Payments as a core growth engine for FreshBooks, this leader is accountable for running the Payments business day\-to\-day and delivering in\-year P\&L impact across the Payments and Financial Services Lines of Business.  

This is the operational heart of the LOB, and it is a hands\-on, player\-coach role. The Director owns the rhythm of the business, drives cross\-functional execution across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Support, and Risk, and makes the trade\-offs between customer experience, operational feasibility, risk exposure, and financial performance. They translate multi\-year strategy into quarterly delivery, hold teams accountable for measurable results, and intervene decisively when the numbers require a course correction — while personally rolling up their sleeves on execution, not just directing it.  

The ideal candidate is a deep payments operator ready to grow into full commercial ownership — analytically rigorous, commercially sharp, and a confident executive communicator — who does the work rather than only delegating it, and who can own delivery on the biggest bets (surcharging, repricing, embedded product expansion) while keeping the day\-to\-day machine running.

**What you'll do**

#### **Run the Payments Business — Operating Rhythm, Metrics, and Delivery**

* Own the operating rhythm: weekly business reviews (WBR), monthly business reviews (MBR), monthly P\&L reviews, and the monthly KPI report in partnership with FP\&A and Data \& Analytics.
* Own the TPV and revenue forecast as source of truth; monitor performance against net revenue, TPV, and net Payments\-attached\-user targets, and drive the actions to close gaps.
* Translate performance insights into clear, executive\-ready recommendations and deliver them in leadership and cross\-LOB forums.

#### **Drive Execution on Priority Initiatives**

* Lead delivery on the highest\-value Payments initiatives — surcharging, repricing, AutoPay phases, Optimized Payments / interchange work, and launch readiness for BNPL and embedded partners (Klarna, Cash App, Affirm, Embedded IPO).
* Manage the Payments portfolio: prioritize across initiatives, influence resource allocation, and hold cross\-functional partners accountable for delivery, results, and learnings.
* Challenge or adjust decisions that could limit business impact — default configurations, pricing changes, rollout sequencing.

#### **Own Payment Operations Execution**

* Own the operational backbone hands\-on: payouts and reconciliation health, processor and payout workflows (e.g., Stripe Connect), and the automation that reduces cost, errors, and support volume.
* Oversee 1099 operations, compliance reviews, and PayFac sub\-merchant controls (chargeback, fraud, merchant\-default monitoring).
* Own vendor and partner onboarding and operational performance — uptime, SLAs, and adherence to payment security and compliance standards.

#### **Own Partner, Vendor, and Network Relationships**

* Manage the day\-to\-day relationship with Stripe (monthly ops, accelerator program, QBRs) as the most active external surface.
* Support and execute partner and vendor negotiations across BNPL providers, processors, and card networks (Visa, Mastercard, Discover), escalating strategic terms to the GM.
* Steward external advisor and consultant engagements supporting CoGS, pricing, and PMM work.

#### **Own High\-Value Customer and Commercial Decisions**

* Own the high\-value customer strategy, including strategic account pricing and repricing initiatives.
* Set and enforce pricing within guardrails; recommend guardrail changes and escalate significant exceptions to the GM.
* Balance customer growth against margin discipline and PayFac sub\-merchant risk exposure.

#### **Partner and Influence Across the Organization**

* Serve as a trusted business partner to leaders across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Support, and Risk, driving outcomes through cadence and influence rather than direct authority.
* Chair the Payments leadership forums (monthly leadership review, bi\-weekly POD leadership) and represent the business in cross\-LOB and executive forums.

#### **Manage Risk, Compliance, and Market Intelligence**

* Partner with Risk and Finance on risk strategy and guardrails; oversee compliance reviews and regulatory obligations.
* Track the payments and fintech ecosystem — competitive threats, network and regulatory shifts — and translate signals into near\-term action and forward strategy.

#### *

jobs.description:
**Date Posted:** 11/02/2026  

**Req ID:**50757  

**Faculty/Division:** Faculty of Arts \& Science  

**Department:** Faculty Budget, Planning and Finance  

**Campus**: St. George (Downtown Toronto)  

**Existing Vacancy:** Yes

  


**Description:**

**About Us**

  



The Faculty of Arts \& Science is the heart of Canada’s leading university and one of the most comprehensive and diverse academic divisions in the world. The strength of Arts \& Science derives from our combined teaching and research excellence in the humanities, sciences and social sciences across 29 departments, seven colleges and 46 interdisciplinary centres, institutes and programs. We can only realize our mission with the dedication and excellence of engaged staff and faculty. The diversity of opportunities and perspectives within the Faculty reflect the local and global landscape and the need for curiosity, innovative thinking and collaboration. At Arts \& Science, we take pride in our legacy of innovation and discovery that has changed the way we think about the world.

  


**Position Summary**

  



The Director, Financial and Business Analytics works independently under the general direction of the Executive Director, Budget, Planning and Finance to develop and implement financial and accounting procedures, develop budget models, develop financial control procedures and ensure compliance with financial and accounting policies. The incumbent manages and produces complex data analysis relating to administrative matters across the Faculty of Arts \& Science and provides related advanced financial/financial management recommendations and advice. In collaboration with the Manager, Faculty Budget \& Finance the incumbent develops and implements annual budget and financial processes.



The incumbent reviews existing financial/administrative models, analyzes new programs and initiatives, calculates costs, prepares and audits financial models for completeness and viability, prepares and analyzes financial statements and reports using in depth knowledge of the Faculty and University planning environment. The incumbent plays an active role in the development and implementation of the Faculty of Arts \& Science strategic short and long range budget plans and models. The incumbent performs operational/departmental audits and makes financial and business recommendations based on findings, including making recommendations on organizational restructuring, enabling data\-driven leadership of organizational change within units of the Faculty.



The incumbent directly manages the Faculty’s business processes for the Dean’s Office portfolios, including the management of the Business Officer, and business support staff. This role is responsible for establishing best practice for business processes in the decanal portfolios and the broader Faculty business community.

  


**Essential Qualifications**

  


**Education**



University degree and completion of a recognized professional accounting program (CMA, CGA, or CA), or equivalent combination of education and experience

  


**Experience**



Minimum 8 years of related budgeting, accounting and financial analysis experience in a higher education environment, a large public sector setting or a large complex environment. Significant experience with university based administrative management systems (FIS, HRIS, and RIS) and with University budgeting/financial policies and procedures. Experience supervising staff in a unionized environment.

  


**Skills**



* Advanced personal computer skills, particularly Excel and Access.
* Advanced knowledge of the University’s Administrative management Systems (FIS, HRIS and RIS).
* Proven ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, to a large and diverse community of stakeholders.
* Effective and creative problem solver, with good judgement.
* Demonstrated ability to plan and execute complex projects and manage conflicting priorities while working toward tight deadlines.
* Able to assess information and make decisions and recommendations regarding matters confidential to labour relations.
* Must have advanced knowledge of Excel, Access, ROSI, Word, AMS systems (FIS \& HRIS).
* Must have an excellent understanding of complex and varied computerized databases, and knowledge of the relevant and capabilities of various methods of retrieving data.
  


**Other**



* Highly detail oriented and accurate with exceptional analytical skills.
* Commitment to providing a high level of service to a large group of stakeholders.
* Ability to take the initiative and respond to change.
* Able to respect matters of a sensitive nature and maintain confidentiality.
* Able to assess information and make decisions and recommendations regarding matters confidential to labour relations.
* Ability to lead and assemble working groups and committees to discuss and assess projects that require input from many stakeholders and provide leadership to guide and oversee their efforts.
* Proven analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
* Must be able to translate statistical and analytical results into easily understood terms.
* Demonstrated commitment to equity and diversity.
* An excellent understanding of the objectives of the Faculty and an ability to effectively achieve the priorities of the Faculty.
  


**Closing Date:** 11/15/2026,11:59PM ET  

**Employee Group:** Salaried  

**Personnel Subarea:**PM  

**Appointment Type**: Budget \- Continuing  

**Schedule:** Full\-Time  

**Pay Scale Group \& Hiring Zone:** PM 6 \- Hiring Zone: $137,645 \- $160,585 \- Broadband Salary Range: $137,645 \- $229,410  

**Job Category:** Finance/Budget/Planning/Audit
